name: Designer Edition!

pick.label: Pick an object
pick.heading: Pick a boring object and give it a designer makeover
lead: Some objects do their job perfectly and nobody has ever looked at them twice. Nobody has ever posted a photo of their cheese grater on Instagram. Yet.
Choose something ordinary and turn it into a designer object that people would pay far too much for. It can work better than before, or it can look amazing and work terribly. *Your choice.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: This is not a real design brief, it’s just for a bit of fun. Your object can be beautiful and useless, useful and ugly, or, if you’re very clever, both.

rows: Which boring object are you giving a makeover?
Ugly, boring, hard to use, always lost, a bit disgusting…
What does it look like now? Materials, colours, shape, a fancy name if you like.
Better than before, worse, or not at all? Be honest.
Who buys it, and where do they buy it?
I would show it off by:
A shop window, a museum, an influencer, a famous kitchen…

values.problem: It’s ugly, it’s a bit gross, and it sits next to the sink where everybody can see it.
values.makeover: La Spazzola: a hand-blown glass handle, brass bristles and its own little marble stand. It comes with a certificate.
values.works: Not really. The brass scratches the pans and the handle is too short to reach the bottom of a glass. But it looks fantastic on the windowsill.
values.who: People with enormous open-plan kitchens in Mitte who order a takeaway every night anyway.
values.show: A pop-up shop on Torstraße with one single brush in the window, lit like a diamond. No price tag. If you have to ask, you can’t afford it.

yours.label: Your makeover
yours.heading: Your design
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your designer object in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which makeover wins?
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their designer object in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
